newsitem.title: USA: Late NYMEX Hub natgas still holds gains with cash.
newsitem.headline: Late NYMEX Hub natgas still holds gains with cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained mostly higher late Wednesday in moderate trade, with blistering heat over much of the nation keeping physical and paper prices fairly firm, market sources said.
At 1405 EDT, August climbed 3.8 cents to $2.20 per million British thermal units, while September was 1.9 cents higher at $2.175. Most others remained unchanged to up two cents.

"Cash has picked up every day this week, but I'm not sure how much more upside there is. I think it will ease back as soon as the weather cools," said one Texas-based trader, noting forecasts for later in the week and for next week were calling for more seasonal weather in the eastern U.S.
Chart traders also showed some skepticism, noting that this week's decline in open interest as prices rose was a sign the rally was more short covering than new buying.
They still pegged major resistance in August along the down trendline at $2.23, with support in the $2.15 area and then at last week's low of $2.051.

In the cash Wednesday, Gulf Coast gas firmed a couple of cents to about the $2.20 area. Midcon pipes were steady to up slightly at $2.10-13. New York city gate gas also gained a couple of cents to the mid-to-high $2.50s.
A Reuter poll of industry players showed most expected an 85-95 bcf weekly stock build when AGA data are released later today. For the same week last year, stocks gained 94 bcf.
NYMEX said 19,917 contracts traded at 1335 EDT.
On the KCBT, August climbed four cents to $2.10, while deferreds were one to 2.5 cents higher. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.2 cent to 10.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
